title: Monetary Policy Report—July 2024
summary: The Bank of Canada reduced its overnight rate target by 25 basis points to 4½%. The Bank projects core inflation to ease to approximately 2.5% in the second half of 2024 and CPI inflation to return sustainably to the 2% target later in 2025, with risks to the outlook considered balanced.
key_points: Bank of Canada reduced overnight rate target by 25 bps to 4½%, with Bank Rate at 4¾% and deposit rate at 4½%
Continuing balance sheet normalization as part of monetary policy framework
Core inflation expected to ease to about 2.5% in H2 2024, with gradual decline thereafter
CPI inflation forecast to temporarily fall below core inflation due to gasoline prices before rising modestly into H1 2025
US economic growth slowing after surprising strength; euro area expanding after stalling in 2023
Upside risks: services price inflation persistence, global geopolitical tensions; Downside risks: weaker household spending, slower global growth
Wage growth remains elevated; services inflation most affected by wages proving persistent
why_it_matters: This Bank of Canada rate cut signals the central bank's confidence that inflation is on a sustainable path toward target. The balanced risk assessment suggests a measured approach to further easing, with markets watching closely for subsequent cuts as economic conditions evolve.
macro_context: The Canadian economy shows excess supply with weak consumer spending per capita and subdued residential investment. Population growth has increased labor supply and cooled the labor market. The Bank projects economic strengthening in H2 2024 and into 2025, driven by export growth and household spending as borrowing costs decline. Global growth projected at around 3% with US slowdown offsetting euro area recovery.
market_structure_context: The Bank continues its balance sheet normalization policy alongside the rate cut, indicating continued unwinding of quantitative easing-era holdings.
